name: Mendel’s inheritance patterns in peas
description: Mendel described stable patterns of dominant and recessive characters across pea generations and interpreted them as inheritance through discrete factors.

date.basis: The cited historical account supports 1865; this is a dated documented episode, not proof of global priority.

events.statement: Mendel presented his plant hybridization work to the Brünn Natural History Society in February and March 1865.

evidence.supports: Mendel’s 1865 presentations, studied inheritance patterns and approximately three-to-one second-generation ratios.
Limits the scope: many traits show more complex inheritance.

contributions.resource: Studied pea characters and presented the inheritance findings in 1865.

evidence.supports: Attributes studied pea inheritance and 1865 presentations to Mendel.

date.basis: Date of this specific publication or contemporary episode, not the date of the original discovery.

events.statement: Mendel’s paper appeared in the Brünn Natural History Society’s yearbook in 1866; the manuscript also bears a note ordering 40 copies for him, whose date the cited account does not specify.

evidence.supports: The manuscript account identifies publication, Niessl’s role and a note ordering 40 copies; it does not date the order.

evidence.supports: Describes the society’s 1865 lectures and the later paper.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established by the evidence collected here for this scoped achievement, not a claim of absolute priority.

caveats: The ratios concern the particular characters studied; many traits have more complex inheritance. Mendel did not identify DNA as the carrier.
